chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated to me from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

"There is no salat (prayer) except with taharah, and three stones suffice you for istinjaʾ, and upon that the sunnah (prophetic tradition) from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله has proceeded. As for urine, it is indispensable that it be washed."
As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who remembered, while he was in his salat (prayer), that he had not performed istinjaʾ after relieving himself. He said: "He should turn away, perform istinjaʾ after relieving himself, and repeat the salat. But if he remembers after he has finished his salat, that suffices him and no repetition is required of him."

So the correct way of understanding it here as well is what we mentioned: that he remembered that he had not performed istinjaʾ with water, even though he had performed istinjaʾ with stone. In that case, it is recommended for him to leave the salat, as long as he is still in it, then perform istinjaʾ with water and repeat the salat. But if he has already finished it, then nothing is upon him. If he had not performed istinjaʾ at all, then repeating the salat would have been obligatory upon him in every case, whether he turned away or did not turn away, as we have explained; and what follows further clarifies that.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the established prophetic tradition and normative practice
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine, for which washing is specifically required
key_terms.بِطَهُورٍ: with ritual purity required for the validity of salat
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَحْجَارٍ: three stones used as a sufficient means of istinjaʾ in the stated case
key_terms.غَسْلِهِ: washing it, meaning cleansing the urine impurity with water
key_terms.يُعِيدُ الصَّلَاةَ: he repeats the salat due to a defect related to taharah

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about istinjaʾ with stones or water and repeating salat if one forgot?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the rulings of taharah as they relate to salat, especially the sufficiency of using three stones for istinjaʾ and the necessity of washing urine. It also addresses the case of one who remembers during or after salat that he did not perform istinjaʾ, distinguishing between complete omission and omission of washing with water specifically. The passage reflects juristic reconciliation between narrations and the practice established from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
